results.summary: Frogger is a hardware clone of the arcade game Frogger rendered procedurally to a 640x480 VGA display with no framebuffer, multipliers or dividers. It uses a Psychogenic Gamepad PMOD as its primary input, falling back to direct up/down/left/right buttons on ui_in[3:0], and outputs 1-bit square-wave sound effects via a DDS phase accumulator. The screen is partitioned into 15 rows of 32 pixels, with the top rows showing lives and score, and the river lanes featuring drifting logs at varying speeds. The design is notable for its fully procedural per-pixel graphics at the VGA pixel clock, avoiding any frame buffer or complex arithmetic.

This project is a Physically Unclonable Function (PUF) based on ring oscillator (RO) frequency comparisons. It uses an array of ring oscillators and compares their frequencies to generate a unique chip-specific response. The design is controlled via SPI and includes a PRNG for challenge generation. It is notable for its use of analog frequency variations to create a hardware security primitive.

This design is a 9-channel oscillator frequency counter with programmable gate time, controlled over I2C and supplemented by SPI DAC outputs and SPI ADC sampling. It measures the frequency of up to nine external oscillators and provides analog output via a DAC and digital input via an ADC. The design is intended for instrumentation and industrial monitoring applications. It is notable for its multi-channel measurement capability and flexible control interface.

This is an analog phase-locked loop targeting a 2.4 GHz output, including a bandgap reference for the charge pump. The design uses a VCO and charge pump to generate a high-frequency clock signal. It is implemented at the transistor level and is intended for RF applications. The design is notable for its analog implementation of a frequency synthesizer.

This project is a VGA 640x480 @ 60 Hz display controller that outputs a 1-bit sigma-delta modulated audio signal. It generates a test pattern on the VGA output and produces a simple tone through the audio output. The design is intended for testing VGA and audio interfaces. It is notable for its simple implementation of video and audio generation.

The Lambda Clock is a highly-optimized full digital calendar and clock built for a 10-digit 7-segment multiplexed display architecture using three cascaded 74HC595 shift registers. It includes a BCD-native limit handling to avoid binary-to-BCD resource explosion. The design features a buzzer output and is controlled via a finite state machine. It is notable for its efficient BCD-based timekeeping and display driving.

This project is a digital circuit that implements a sequence detector for a specific bit pattern. It uses a finite state machine to recognize the pattern on a serial input. The design is verified with a cocotb testbench. It is notable for its simple and clear implementation of a sequence detection algorithm.

This project is a hardware implementation of a simple calculator with a keypad input and a 7-segment display output. It supports basic arithmetic operations such as addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division. The design uses a finite state machine to manage the calculation process. It is notable for its compact implementation of a calculator on a chip.

This project is a digital circuit that implements a pseudo-random number generator using a linear feedback shift register (LFSR). It produces a sequence of pseudo-random bits based on a seed value. The design is intended for use in games or other applications requiring random numbers. It is notable for its simple and efficient LFSR-based implementation.

This project is a hardware implementation of a simple processor with a custom instruction set. It includes an ALU, register file, and control logic. The design is written in Verilog and is intended for educational purposes. It is notable for its minimalistic yet complete CPU architecture.
